simplified_takeaways: Returns look strong if build costs stay low, but current CAPEX is 30% below market — this is a risk.
QIA-Brookfield partnership makes financing easier and faster if a government anchor is secured.
Grid connection and transformer delivery are the main schedule risks; both take about 24 months.
Most revenue will come from a single government tenant at first, which is efficient but risky.
The design allows for future expansion if demand stays strong.
explainability.why_this_recommendation: We recommend proceeding with a 50 MW powered shell in Qatar, using a Tier III+ design and hybrid cooling, because this approach balances speed, cost, and operational risk. This is supported by recent Equinix and Digital Realty filings showing strong margins and occupancy for similar assets, and by live signals confirming that demand and pricing are robust in the region. The main risk is that the current CAPEX estimate is materially below market benchmarks; this must be reconciled before final investment. The QIA-Brookfield partnership and government anchor tenant de-risk financing and ramp, but customer concentration and supply chain delays remain key watchpoints.

signals.title: KAHRAMAA 50 MW grid connection: 24-month process — must run in parallel, not series
signals.implication: Sequencing KAHRAMAA application after QFZA permit adds 24 months to the critical path — a developer error that is responsible for the majority of Qatar DC delays. Parallel processing (KAHRAMAA + QFZA simultaneously) delivers both approvals by mid-2027 for a Q3 2025 submission. Serial sequencing slips energisation to 2029.

signals.implication: A Qatar powered-shell or JV at 50–200 MW with Tier III+ and delivery within 30 months of LOI is directly financeable. Global DC wholesale vacancy is at 3%; demand is outpacing supply in every constrained market.
